decisive_items: Initial serum troponin I level: 6.18 ng/mL
ECG Findings: Normal sinus rhythm, ST-segment elevations with PR-segment depression in leads II, III, and aVF, ST-segment depression in lead V1, and PR-segment elevation in lead aVR
response.rationale: Young man with prodromal viral symptoms, elevated troponin, diffuse ST elevation with PR depression, and normal coronaries strongly favors myocarditis over pericarditis (which typically has lower troponin) and ACS (excluded by normal coronaries).

rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries contradict acute coronary syndrome despite elevated troponin.
ECG pattern fits pericarditis but significant troponin elevation and myocardial involvement favor myocarditis.
